report.tagline: A visual search and saving app where people find ideas for outfits, homes, recipes and events, and then buy the products in them.
report.simpleSummary: Pinterest is like a giant digital pinboard. You search for something like 'small balcony ideas' or 'wedding mehendi outfits', and you get a wall of pictures. You save the ones you like to boards, and many pictures link to a shop where you can buy what you see. Pinterest is free and makes almost all its money by showing ads that look like normal pins.

overview.whatItDoes: Pinterest helps people find and save ideas using pictures instead of words. Users search or scroll a personalised feed, save 'Pins' to boards, and click through to buy products or read recipes and guides. Brands pay to put their products in front of people who are planning a purchase.
howItWorks: Users type a search or tap a picture to find visually similar ideas, using Pinterest Lens and visual search.
Users save Pins to boards like 'Living room' or 'Goa trip', which tells Pinterest exactly what they plan to do.
The home feed recommends new Pins based on what each person saved, searched and clicked.
Shoppable Pins link to product pages on retailer sites, with price and stock pulled from the retailer's catalogue.
Advertisers buy Promoted Pins and shopping ads, directly or through partners like Amazon and Google ad tools.
AI features like the Pinterest Assistant and 'Top Boards' help users go from inspiration to a shopping list.
overview.valueProposition: For users: a calm, positive place to plan your life with pictures, without the pressure of posting or follower counts. For advertisers: reach people while they are still deciding what to buy, before they have picked a brand.

personas.name: The Gen Z style planner
personas.description: A 21-year-old college student who uses Pinterest to build outfit boards, room makeovers and mood boards, and calls it her 'vision board'.
goals: Find a personal style and ideas to copy
Buy similar items within a student budget
frustrations: AI-generated images that show products which do not exist
Shoppable links that go to dead or overpriced pages

personas.name: The home and event planner
personas.description: A 34-year-old planning a home renovation or a wedding, saving hundreds of Pins over months.
goals: Collect ideas in one place and share boards with a partner or designer
Turn saved ideas into a real shopping list
frustrations: Pins without a source, so they cannot find the actual product
Feeds that keep showing the same ideas after the project is done

personas.name: The everyday recipe saver
personas.description: A busy parent who searches 'easy dinner' or 'high protein breakfast' on Pinterest every week.
goals: Find quick recipes that actually work
frustrations: Recipe Pins that link to blogs full of pop-ups

personas.name: The retail advertiser
personas.description: A marketing manager at a home decor or fashion brand who buys shopping ads on Pinterest alongside Meta and Google.
goals: Reach people early while they plan a purchase
Get sales at a cost that beats other ad platforms
frustrations: Weaker sales tracking than Meta or Google
Cutting budgets when tariffs squeeze margins

painPoints.pain: It is hard to describe a style or design in words for a normal search engine.
painPoints.howSolved: Visual search and Lens let users search with a picture and get similar looks.

painPoints.pain: Ideas from many websites and screenshots get lost in a phone's gallery.
painPoints.howSolved: Boards keep saved ideas organised by project, and they can be shared with others.

painPoints.pain: Seeing a product in a photo but not knowing where to buy it.
painPoints.howSolved: Shoppable Pins and 'shop the look' link items in a photo to product pages.

painPoints.pain: Most social apps feel stressful, with likes, comments and comparison.
painPoints.howSolved: Pinterest is built for saving, not posting, so most users never share anything publicly.

painPoints.pain: Planning a big project like a wedding takes months and many decisions.
painPoints.howSolved: Boards, sections and collaborators let a project grow over time and be shared with family.

painPoints.pain: Brands find it hard to reach shoppers before they have chosen a brand.
painPoints.howSolved: Users search Pinterest with mostly unbranded queries like 'boho bedroom', so ads reach undecided shoppers.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Lets users save any Pin into themed boards and sections.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Saves are the clearest signal of future intent, which powers both recommendations and ad targeting.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Finds similar Pins and products from a photo or a part of a Pin.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Solves the 'I cannot describe it' problem and is a key reason people choose Pinterest over Google.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Retailers upload product feeds so Pins show price and a buy link.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Moves Pinterest from inspiration to sales, which lets it charge advertisers more.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Shows a never-ending feed of Pins ranked by what each user likes.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Brings users back daily even when they are not searching, which creates more ad space.

coreFeatures.feature: Gen AI labels and 'see fewer AI Pins' control
coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Tags AI-generated images and lets users reduce them in their feed.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Protects trust after a wave of user anger about AI slop, meaning low-quality AI-made content.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Automated ad tools, and access to Pinterest ads through Amazon DSP, Google DV360 and Yahoo DSP.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Makes buying Pinterest ads easier, so it can win budget from bigger platforms.

businessModel.summary: Pinterest makes almost all its money from ads. Users pay nothing. Advertisers pay when users see or click Promoted Pins and shopping ads. The US and Canada bring in most of the money, because an American user is worth far more to advertisers than a user in India or Brazil.

revenueStreams.detail: Ads that look like normal Pins in search and the feed, sold by clicks, views or sales goals. This is nearly all revenue.
Amazon and other partners fill some of Pinterest's ad slots, especially outside the US, and Pinterest gets a share.
Big advertisers buy Pinterest ads through Amazon DSP, Google DV360 and Yahoo DSP, rolled out more widely in 2026.

businessModel.pricing: Free for users. Ads are sold by auction, so there is no public rate card. Advertisers set daily or campaign budgets.
costDrivers: Cloud servers and storage for billions of images
AI and machine learning staff and computing for recommendations and visual search
Sales and marketing to win advertisers
businessModel.unitEconomics: Pinterest earns about $7 per year from an average user worldwide ($1.17 billion a quarter across 661 million users, times four). The gap by region is huge: a US or Canadian user is worth roughly $25 to $30 a year, while a 'rest of world' user brings in around $1 to $3. Serving a user costs only a small part of this, mainly servers and AI. Pinterest keeps about 29 cents of each dollar as adjusted EBITDA. So the money game is to grow revenue per user in rich markets and slowly lift it everywhere else.

howTheyGetUsers: Google image and web search, where Pins rank for millions of 'ideas' queries
Shared boards and Pins sent on WhatsApp, iMessage and Instagram
Browser save button and links from blogs and shops
Word of mouth among Gen Z, now the largest age group on the app
whatBringsUsersBack: Ongoing projects like weddings, home moves and seasonal outfits
Personalised home feed that updates with each save
Push and email notifications with ideas based on boards
Seasonal search spikes like Halloween, Diwali decor and Christmas
growth.moat: Pinterest has more than a decade of data on what hundreds of millions of people save and plan to do, linked to billions of images. Each save teaches its system what goes with what. A rival can copy the grid layout, but not that history of intent, or the habit of 'I go to Pinterest to plan'.

competitors.name: Instagram
competitors.positioning: Meta's photo and video app, with explore, saves and shopping ads.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Instagram is about people and posting. Pinterest is about ideas and planning, with less social pressure and more search.

competitors.name: TikTok
competitors.positioning: Short video feed that drives trends and TikTok Shop sales.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: TikTok is entertainment first. Pinterest users come with a project in mind and save for later.

competitors.name: Google Search and Lens
competitors.positioning: General search engine with image search and shopping results.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Pinterest adds boards, a feed and taste-based recommendations, not just one-off answers.

competitors.name: Amazon
competitors.positioning: The biggest online store and a fast-growing ad business.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Amazon captures people ready to buy. Pinterest catches them earlier, while they are still choosing, and even partners with Amazon on ads.

competitors.name: AI chat assistants like ChatGPT
competitors.positioning: Answer 'what should I wear or buy' questions and now show products.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Pinterest is visual and personal over time. Chatbots are text-first and forget your taste unless you tell them.

northStar.metric: Weekly users who save or click through on at least one Pin
northStar.why: A save or a click to a shop means Pinterest helped someone move a real plan forward. It shows value to users, and it is also what advertisers pay for.

improvementIdeas.idea: Make 'Real only' a one-tap feed filter that removes AI-labelled Pins, and default it on for decor and recipe searches.
improvementIdeas.problem: Users are angry about AI slop and lose trust in what they save.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher save rate and fewer complaints in key categories.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Save rate per search in decor and recipes

improvementIdeas.idea: Add a 'find this exact item' button that checks every saved product Pin weekly and shows live price and stock.
improvementIdeas.problem: Many Pins have dead links or no source, so shoppers cannot buy.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More outbound clicks and better ad results for retailers.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Outbound clicks per 1,000 product Pin views

improvementIdeas.idea: Board-to-cart: turn a whole board into a shopping list with prices from several shops.
improvementIdeas.problem: Planners save dozens of ideas but buying them one by one is slow.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More purchases per user and a reason for advertisers to spend more.

improvementIdeas.idea: Human review fast lane for appeals on accounts older than one year.
improvementIdeas.problem: Wrongful AI bans anger loyal creators and users.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer lost creators and less bad press.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Median appeal resolution time and reinstatement rate

improvementIdeas.idea: Simpler sales measurement for small advertisers, with a guided conversions API setup in Shopify.
improvementIdeas.problem: Advertisers cut Pinterest first because they cannot prove sales.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More ad spend retained when budgets tighten.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of ad spend with conversion tracking

pmLessons: Intent is valuable. Pinterest earns money because users tell it what they plan to do, not just what they watch.
User growth does not equal revenue growth. Most new users are in markets where ads pay little, so monetisation per region matters.
AI can hurt a product as fast as it helps. Letting AI images flood the feed damaged trust, and Pinterest had to add labels and controls.
Measurement is a product. Advertisers spend where they can prove results, so ad tracking tools directly drive revenue.

interviewQuestions.question: Pinterest's users hit a record but revenue growth slowed. Why, and what would you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Split revenue into users times revenue per user, by region. Show growth is in low-paying markets. Suggest ways to lift revenue per user: shopping, measurement, partners.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you deal with AI-generated content on Pinterest?
interviewQuestions.hint: Separate harmful (fake products, spam) from fine (creative art). Discuss labels, user controls, ranking changes and creator rules. Pick metrics like save rate and trust surveys.

interviewQuestions.question: What should Pinterest's north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Argue for an action that shows real value, like weekly savers or clickers. Explain why time spent is wrong for a planning product. Add guardrails.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to help a Gen Z user go from a mood board to a purchase.
interviewQuestions.hint: Clarify the user and budget. Map the journey from save to buy. Propose a feature, then say how you would test it and measure it.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Pinterest in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at low ad rates, local languages, festive and wedding planning, and shopping partners like Myntra or Flipkart. Say how you would make money, not just add users.
